[SAFER Walls News] racingmadesafer.com SAFER (Steel and Foam Energy Reduction) Midwest Roadside Safety Facility ESPN.com - The SAFER barrier explained NASCAR.com - SAFER Barrier construction IndyCar - Fan Info - INDYCAR 101 - Safety - SAFER Barrier Motorsport - SAFER (Steel And Foam Energy Reduction) wall presentation Jayski.com's SAFER Past News Archive Latest News Dover extending SAFER barriers and increasing usable space in Cup garage: Dover International Speedway has started two construction projects which will add more than 500 feet of SAFER barriers around the track and increase usable space for NASCAR haulers in the NASCAR Sprint Cup Series garage. Both projects are scheduled to be completed in time for the Sept. 30-Oct. 2 NASCAR tripleheader weekend at the Monster Mile, highlighted by the first elimination race of the 2016 Chase for the NASCAR Sprint Cup Series championship playoffs on Sunday, Oct. 2. Facts on the recent construction are: o Approximately 500 feet of Steel And Foam Energy Reduction (SAFER) barriers will be added to the one-mile, high-banked, concrete oval. The outside wall in Turn 2, under the walkover bridge, and the outside wall of Turn 4, entering the frontstretch, will now include SAFER barriers. All of the SAFER barriers will be added to existing walls. o The installation companies are Kent Construction of Smyrna, Del., and North Industrial Machine of Hartsville, SC. o A 753-foot-long concrete wall separating the NASCAR Sprint Cup Series garage area from the existing harness racing track is being added. The 10-foot-high wall will stretch from the Infield Media Center to the end of the NASCAR Sprint Cup Series garage, removing the grass hill between the garage area and harness track that was in place. o The new construction will allow for additional space for each NASCAR hauler to park in the NASCAR Sprint Cup Series garage, and will create a safer environment in the area. o The installation company is Kent Construction of Smyrna, Del. [UAE's Asif Khan handed 15-month ban for using a banned substance] Asif Khan swings one away ICC/Getty Images Cricinfo staff Multiple Authors Aug 27, 2026, 05:07 AM ET Email Print Open Extended Reactions Asif Khan , the UAE batter, has been banned for 15 months after admitting to having tested positive for a banned substance - "a metabolite of mesterolone" - in an out-of-competition test conducted in September 2025, the ICC said in a statement on Thursday. The statement said that Asif, 36, "had admitted the violation" of Article 2.1 of the ICC's anti-doping code and accepted the period of ineligibility "pursuant to a case resolution agreement entered into with the World Anti-Doping Agency and the ICC", which means there is no right to appeal on the part of the player. The sanction is effective from September 8, 2025 and will run until December 7, 2026. "Asif may return to training with a team or use the facilities of a club or other ICC Member organisation from 8 October 2026 but will only be eligible to play from 8 December," the statement added. "The player's individual results from 8 September 2025 until his provisional suspension on 29 December 2025 have been disqualified, along with all resulting consequences, including the loss of any medals, points, prize money or prizes." Asif, a former Pakistan Under-19 cricketer, made his UAE debut in March 2022 in an ODI against Oman in the ICC's Cricket World Cup League 2. He turned out in 38 ODIs and 56 T20Is between then and September 2025. The last three of those T20Is, against India, Oman and Pakistan in the T20 Asia Cup in 2025, came after September 8, and will be removed from his record.
